title: Vishal Garg Ousted as Better CEO, Vows Legal Fight to Reclaim His Company
excerpt: The Indian-origin founder of AI mortgage lender Better Home & Finance says he was 'hoodwinked' out of the company he built, and is now demanding his return as CEO — offering to work for $1 a year until profitability.
body:
• Vishal Garg, the Indian-origin founder of AI mortgage lender Better Home & Finance, was ousted as CEO on August 3 after a newly appointed board member convinced directors to remove him within a week of joining.
  • Better's valuation has cratered from $8 billion during the pandemic to roughly $300 million, with the company losing over $1 billion since going public via SPAC in 2023.
  • Garg has retained prominent attorney Alex Spiro and is demanding reinstatement, offering to work for $1 per year until the company reaches profitability.
  • The stock has fallen 45% since the leadership change, with Garg claiming his Class B shares give him enough votes to force his return.

Vishal Garg built Better Home & Finance into one of the most talked-about fintech companies in the country. Then he destroyed its reputation with a Zoom layoff of 900 people. Then he tried to rebuild it with AI. Now the board has kicked him out — and he's fighting to get back in.

Garg, the Indian-origin founder and longtime CEO of the AI-powered mortgage lender, was removed from his position on August 3, according to CNN and Inman. Daniel Lewis, a former hedge fund manager who founded Orange Capital, was named interim CEO. The company described the transition as a "mutual agreement." Garg says he was fired.

A One-Week Boardroom Coup

The speed of Garg's ouster was striking. Lewis joined Better's board on July 27. One week later, he had convinced the board to remove the founder and install himself as CEO.

https://x.com/CNNnews18/status/2088813398515675519

Garg told CNN he felt "hoodwinked" by the move. He has since retained Alex Spiro of Quinn Emanuel — the high-profile litigator known for representing Elon Musk and Jay-Z — and sent a letter to the board demanding his return as CEO.

"We're winning. We've tripled loan volume. We're close to profitability."

— Vishal Garg, ousted Better CEO

In a conciliatory gesture that doubles as a negotiating tactic, Garg has offered to work for $1 per year until Better reaches profitability. He also claims his Class B shares carry special voting powers that give him enough votes to win a board fight.

The Rise, Fall, and Fall Again

Better's trajectory reads like a cautionary tale of pandemic-era fintech excess. The company rode the refinancing boom to $1.5 billion in revenue in 2021 and an $8 billion valuation. Then interest rates rose, volume collapsed, and revenue plunged to $70 million by 2023.

Garg became a national punchline in December 2021 when he fired 900 employees on a single Zoom call. "If you're on this call, you are part of the unlucky group," he told them. He took a leave of absence, survived a whistleblower lawsuit that was later dropped, weathered an SEC investigation that led nowhere, and pushed the company through a SPAC merger in August 2023 that saw its stock crater 93%.

Through it all, Garg bet on an AI-driven turnaround. He trained models for faster mortgage processing and signed partnerships with Intuit, Coinbase, OpenAI, and Neo Home Loans. Revenue has recovered to a $200 million annual pace in 2026, and funded loan volume grew 45% year over year in the second quarter. But the company still lost $30.6 million in Q2, and cumulative losses since the SPAC exceed $1 billion.

The Market's Verdict

Investors have not welcomed the change. Better's stock fell 12% on the announcement of Garg's departure and another 7.6% in after-hours trading. Since Lewis took over, shares have declined 45%, bringing the company's market capitalization to roughly $300 million — a fraction of its pandemic peak.

Lewis himself struck a nuanced tone on X shortly after the transition. "There was never a $BETR without @vishal_better," he posted on August 4. "That demands respect."

What Comes Next

The battle lines are drawn. Garg has the legal firepower, the voting shares, and the founder's narrative. The board has control of daily operations and, for now, the CEO title. Board chair Harit Talwar will likely face pressure from both sides as Garg pushes for a resolution.

For the Indian-American tech community, the saga is a vivid reminder of how quickly founder control can evaporate — even when you own the votes, the vision, and the scars from nearly losing it all before.
nri_angle: Vishal Garg's saga at Better is one of the most dramatic boardroom battles involving an Indian-origin tech founder in recent years, following an already turbulent tenure that included a viral mass layoff and a disastrous SPAC merger.
author: Diaspora Desk
